correctness.rationale: Independent path spin sums give W± proportional to products of (1±sign_i t^length_i). The numerator exactly factors as -2 t^2(1-t^2)^2(1+t^2+t^4) Q(t), verified by integer polynomial arithmetic. The Möbius root transformation gives coefficients with exactly two sign changes, bounding positive roots by two, and strict exact rational sign evaluations at 7/10,3/4,4/5 guarantee two different roots. For all 9≤d<e, positivity at 3/4 persists by monotonicity of atanh(t^length) in negative long-path lengths, while high/low-temperature signs remain negative, forcing two crossings. Three-path comparison uses a simple boundary root at t=1 and Descartes. Finite enumeration and executable code confirm exact formulas but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Frustrated finite Ising networks exhibit entropic competition between paths. Unlike the known single crossing in a one-negative-edge decorated bond, an equal absolute coupling graph (no field or higher-order terms) shows an exactly certified negative-positive-negative terminal correlation as temperature varies. The result proves the effect in an infinite graph family and shows it cannot occur among three or fewer simple parallel paths. These are physically interpretable sharp sign-transition facts, not simply a numerical approximation, arbitrary normalization check, or known ring-table recomputation.
